questions_and_answers.question_text: How is age normally expressed in Italian?

answers.answer_text: How many children do they have?

questions_and_answers.question_text: What does "far vedere qualcosa a qualcuno" mean?
What does "non vedere l'ora di" express?

answers.answer_text: Not to be able to wait to

questions_and_answers.question_text: When is the present subjunctive used after "sperare"?

answers.answer_text: When the subject of sperare is different from the subject of the subjunctive verb
When both subjects are the same

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is used if the subjects are the same after "sperare"?
What can the future tense indicate besides future time?
How is the future tense normally formed for most verbs?
What preposition does a form of "contento" require before an infinitive?

articles.text:
1. Age-asking or age-giving is expressed in Italian by using the verb avere Uto
have. U Thus:
Quanti anni hanno?
Marcello ha 11 anni.
Arianna ne ha 9. How old are they?
lit., How many years do they have?
Marcello is 11 years o/d.
lit., Marcello has 11 years.
Arianna is 9.
lit., Arianna has 9 of them.
2. The dia/og contains several interesting expressions to be learned:
a) far vedere qualcosa a qualcuno to show someone something
ex: Le faccio vedere il Suo ufficio.
l'II show you youroffice.
b) dare su qualcosa to face, look out over something
ex: Le finestre danno sulla piazza.
The windows face the square.
c) non vedere l'ora di ( + infinitive) not to be able to wait to
ex: Non vedo l'ora di cominciare.
J can't wait to begin.
d) trovarsi bene to be comfortable, like it
ex: Spero proprio che vi troviate bene nell'albergo.
I real/y hope that you're comfortable at the hotel.
3. The form vi troviate is a special verb form cal/ed present subjunctive. For ali
verbs it is formed as follows:
mi trovi io farm identical to ~ Lei request farm
si trovi Lei farm identical to
ci troviamo noi farm identical ta ... noi request form
vi troviate voi farm identical to ... noi request form
but with -te in piace
af-mo
si trovino loro form identical to ... loro request form
Examples of the present subjunctive for the three classes of regu/ar verbs
are:
parlare credere
(io) parli
(lei) parli (noi) parliamo
(voi) parliate
(loro) parlino (io) creda
(lei) creda (noi) crediamo
(voi) crediate
(loro) credano
preferire
(io) preferisca
(lei) preferisca (noi) preferiamo
(voi) preferiate
(loro) preferiscano
The present subjunctive is found in certain constructions which will be
pointed out as they occur. The one in the dia/og is:
sperare ... + che ... + present subjunctive
in· which the subject of sperare differs from the subject of the present
subjunctive verbo If the subjects are the same, di + infinitive is used. Thus:
Spero che vi troviate bene nell'albergo.
Spero di trovarmi bene nell'albergo.
4. The future tense form of a verb is frequent/y used to indicate a present
conjecture or probability. Thus:
Andranno a scuola, allora.
They probab/y go to schoo/, then.
They must go to school, then.
They more than likely go to schoo/, then.
5. The future tense is normal/y formed as follows:
(stem) (ending)
io form: .. ò noi form: -emo
infinitive minus-e ~ +--... voi farm: -ete

(lei) crederà credere

preferire

Except for dare, fare, stare, and their compounds (like rifare "to redo "), the
.. a of .. are verbs is ehanged to -e. Thus:

(lei) parlerà parlare
(noi) parleremo
(voi) parlerete

(lei) darà dare
(noi) daremo
{voi} darete

Irregu/ar verb forms (like andranno) are on/y irregular in their stem, never in
their endings. Such verbs will be pointed out as they oeeur.

6. A form of contento Iike (lieto) requires di before an infinitive. Thus:
Siete contenti di essere a Roma?
Are you happy to be in Rome?
